Class ReflectionArguments

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.reflection.ReflectionArguments
public final class ReflectionArguments extends Object
Builds Arguments from the types read reflectively from parameters, fields, return types and type hierarchies, in the shape the annotation processors give the arguments they generate: the raw type, the type arguments recursively, the type variables as GenericPlaceholders, and the annotations of the element and of every level of its type as metadata built by ReflectionAnnotations.

The reverse direction, toType(Argument), renders an argument as a Type for the APIs defined on java.lang.reflect, either keeping an unresolved type variable or rendering it as the type it is bounded by.

Since:
5.2.0
Author:
Denis Stepanov

    • returnOf

      public static Argument<?> returnOf(Method method)
      Converts the return type of a method to an Argument carrying the type-use annotations of the return type. An annotation that targets the method alone belongs to the method, not to its return type; one written before the return type whose target includes TYPE_USE annotates both (JLS 9.7.4), and is on both, as the processors record it.
      Parameters:
      method - The method
      Returns:
      The argument

    • resolveGenericToArgument

      public static <T> @Nullable Argument<T> resolveGenericToArgument(Class<?> type, Class<T> superType)
      Resolves the type arguments a type gives to one of its super types, as an argument of the super type: for a class A extends AbstractList<@Nullable String>, the argument of Collection is Collection<@Nullable String>. The type-use annotations of every extends and implements clause of the hierarchy are carried.
      Type Parameters:
      T - The super type
      Parameters:
      type - The type, an implementation of the super type
      superType - The super type, a class or an interface
      Returns:
      The argument of the super type, or null when the type does not extend or implement it

    • toType

      public static Type toType(Argument<?> argument, boolean typeVariables)
      Renders an argument as a Type, choosing what an unresolved type variable becomes.

      An API that describes a declaration - the type of an injection point, of an observed event - wants the variable itself, so that it can tell List<T> from List<String>; an API that compares types by assignability wants the type the variable is bounded by, which is what the erasure of the declaration yields. The generated metadata carries a GenericPlaceholder for both cases, so the caller says which of the two it means.

      Parameters:
      argument - The argument
      typeVariables - Whether a GenericPlaceholder is rendered as a TypeVariable rather than as the type it is bounded by
      Returns:
      The type
